note:
The three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json (NOT page.research-acetyl-*; the template still carries the Argireline trade name), section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-25: a BEFORE and AFTER of the skin, each half taking exactly half of the 1:1 frame, labelled with the improvement the trial found.

A DELIBERATE BREAK FROM THE COPPER-PEPTIDE AND MATRIXYL PAGES. Those two carry mechanism explainers because their findings are mechanism - collagen synthesis, peptide signalling. Acetyl Hexapeptide-8's three findings are all the SAME KIND of thing: a measured change in the appearance of expression lines, in people, over weeks. So the register changes to a photographic before/after macro. Malcolm was offered the surface-topography and instrument-readout alternatives on 2026-08-25 and chose photographic; the honesty controls below are the conditions that make that defensible, not a hedge against his choice.

THE SPLIT IS THE POINT, AND IT INVERTS THE MATRIXYL RULE. The matrixyl brief barred split frames because these engines render a hard seam down the middle. Here that seam is WANTED: two panels meeting at a crisp vertical edge exactly at the centre of the square. What was a failure mode there is the requested composition here, so `no split screen` / `no dividing line` / `no before and after split` are REMOVED from the negatives. Do not copy the matrixyl negative list wholesale into this wave.

NO LETTERING FROM THE ENGINES - THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING RULE OF THE WAVE. Every percentage, label and citation is composited afterwards by scripts/label-before-after.py at exact pixel positions. The engines are barred from all text. Reason: on this project MATRIXYL failed in ~30 of 50 candidates, and PDRN was resampled into PORN. A garbled efficacy figure is not a cosmetic defect - it is a false clinical claim on a live storefront. A number that cannot be misrendered is a number that was never rendered by a model.

THE AFTER HALF IS BRIEFED TO THE TRIAL'S ACTUAL MAGNITUDE. Each slot states its own degree of change and it is different in each, because the three findings are different sizes: 48.9% > ~30% > 14.6%. The lines must still be PRESENT in every after half - shallower, less shadowed, softer at the edges. An after half showing flawless glass skin would overstate every one of these studies, and 14.6% in particular is a subtle result that must read as subtle. This is an honesty control inside the picture and it is also simply more believable.

MACRO, NOT A PORTRAIT - and that is what makes the diptych possible. The hardest thing in a photographic before/after is the two halves being the same person. At full-face scale the engines render two different women. Cropped tight to the outer eye corner - lashes, lower lid, the temple edge, no mouth, no nose, no hairline - there is far less identity in frame to contradict, and it is also the exact region all three studies photographed (periorbital / crow's feet).

THE MODEL MATCHES THE STUDY POPULATION, PER SLOT. f1 Wang 2013 studied Chinese subjects; f2 Blanes-Mira 2002 European female volunteers; f3 An 2019 Korean female subjects. Matching each frame to its own trial's population is accurate, and it stops one woman appearing to be enrolled in three different studies on one page.

COLOUR: Acetyl's scene colour is Pearl grey D8D6D4 per the concern-to-colour map, exactly as Teal is Matrixyl's and Clinical blue is Copper Peptide's. It is the GROUND behind the skin, not a cast on the skin - the skin stays a natural tone. Copper, teal, clinical blue, champagne and blush are negated by name so this page can never blur with the other four ingredient pages.

SKIN TEXTURE IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST. Judge every candidate at native 1:1 on the skin beside the eye - the exact region where the PDRN hero was rejected on 2026-08-24. Reject the machine crepe: a dense allover field of near-parallel micro-lines at even density with no pore variation. Per the copper-peptide finding this is PER-CANDIDATE, not per-engine, so it must be checked on each frame and never predicted from the supplier.

CLASS B, no references attached. FLUX.2 is in the run - it is barred only from legible branding, and there is none here. Square 2048x2048 to match the other two research pages.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks
slots.prompt:
A single square photograph divided into TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH, meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre of the square. Both panels show THE SAME WOMAN, the same eye, photographed twice from an identical camera position with identical lighting - same face shape, same iris colour, same brow, same lash line, same small skin marks in the same places. Nothing else changes between the two panels except the skin.

The framing is a tight clinical macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE: the lower lid, the lash line, the outer corner itself, and the flat of the temple beside it. The eyebrow is partly in frame at the top. There is no mouth, no nose, no hairline and no ear. The eye is open and relaxed, looking slightly away from the lens, the expression neutral and unsmiling.

She is a Chinese woman in her early forties with clear bare skin and no makeup. The skin is a natural warm tone, finely textured, with real visible pores of varying size, a few faint freckles at irregular intervals, and fine vellus hairs catching the light along the temple.

In the LEFT panel, a fan of expression lines radiates from the outer corner of the eye across the temple: four or five distinct creases, clearly etched, each holding a soft shadow along its length, with finer crepey lines beneath the lower lid. The skin there looks dry-textured and slightly slack.

In the RIGHT panel, THE SAME FAN OF LINES IS STILL CLEARLY PRESENT in the same places and the same number - but each crease is visibly shallower and softer at its edges, holding much less shadow, and the fine crepey texture under the lower lid is smoother and better hydrated. This is a MODERATE, BELIEVABLE improvement, roughly half the depth: the lines have not gone, and the skin is not flawless.

Both panels are lit identically by one soft directional key from the upper left with a gentle fill, raking just enough across the temple to reveal the relief of the skin. The background behind her, softly out of focus, is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4. Shot on a macro lens at a wide aperture, clinical and unretouched, the skin honest and real.
slots.negative_extra: no different woman in the two panels, no mirrored image, no flipped duplicate, no identical untouched copy, no gap between the panels, no white gutter, no seam glow, no smiling, no squinting, no closed eye, no tears, no red eye, no makeup

slots.title: f2 · Blanes-Mira 2002 — up to ~30% reduction in measured wrinkle DEPTH, 30 days
slots.prompt:
A single square photograph divided into TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH, meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre of the square. Both panels show THE SAME WOMAN, the same eye, photographed twice from an identical camera position with identical lighting - same face shape, same iris colour, same brow, same lash line, same small skin marks in the same places. Nothing else changes between the two panels except the skin.

THIS FINDING IS ABOUT DEPTH, SO THE LIGHT IS RAKING. The camera is very close and slightly to the side, so the surface of the skin is seen almost edge-on across the temple and the relief of each line is read by its shadow rather than by its colour.

The framing is a tight clinical macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE and the flat of the temple beside it: lower lid, lash line, outer corner, temple. No mouth, no nose, no hairline, no ear. The eye is open and relaxed, looking away from the lens, the expression neutral and unsmiling.

She is a European woman in her late thirties with clear bare skin and no makeup - a natural fair-to-olive tone, finely textured, with real visible pores of varying size and fine vellus hairs along the temple.

In the LEFT panel, three or four expression lines cross the temple as GROOVES WITH REAL DEPTH: each one carves a distinct V-shaped channel into the surface, catching a bright highlight along its upper wall and holding a dark shadow in its floor, so the relief is unmistakable in the raking light.

In the RIGHT panel, THE SAME GROOVES REMAIN IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, but each is markedly less deep - the channels are shallower, their floors far lighter, the highlight-to-shadow contrast across each one much reduced, so they read as soft depressions rather than cut channels. About a third of the depth is gone. The lines are still visible; the surface is not flat and not perfect.

Both panels are lit identically by one hard low directional key from the left, skimming across the skin at a shallow angle with a single soft fill, so depth is described by shadow. The background behind her, softly out of focus, is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4. Shot on a macro lens, clinical and unretouched.

slots.prompt:
A single square photograph divided into TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH, meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre of the square. Both panels show THE SAME WOMAN, the same eye, photographed twice from an identical camera position with identical lighting - same face shape, same iris colour, same brow, same lash line, same small skin marks in the same places. Nothing else changes between the two panels except the skin.

THIS FINDING IS SMALL AND THE PICTURE MUST BE HONEST ABOUT THAT. The difference between the two panels is SUBTLE - a refinement, not a transformation - and the frame is therefore very tight and very sharp so a small change is still legible.

The framing is an extreme clinical macro of the OUTER CORNER OF ONE EYE: the lash line, the outer canthus and the first few centimetres of temple beside it fill the panel. No mouth, no nose, no hairline, no ear, no eyebrow. The eye is open and relaxed, looking away from the lens, the expression neutral and unsmiling.

She is a Korean woman in her mid thirties with clear bare skin and no makeup - a natural light warm tone, very finely textured, with real visible pores of varying size and fine vellus hairs catching the light.

In the LEFT panel, the skin beside the eye carries a dense network of VERY FINE surface lines - shallow, hairline creases crossing each other in a fine mesh, the surface slightly dry and matte, the texture a little uneven and grainy.

In the RIGHT panel, THE SAME FINE MESH IS STILL THERE and the deeper expression lines are unchanged - but the finest hairline creases are slightly less distinct and slightly fewer, the surface a little more even and better hydrated, with a faint healthy sheen it did not have before. THE CHANGE IS SLIGHT AND MUST LOOK SLIGHT. Anyone comparing the two halves should have to look closely to see it.

Both panels are lit identically by one soft directional key from the upper left with a gentle fill, raking lightly across the skin to reveal fine texture. The background behind her, softly out of focus, is a smooth pale pearl grey, colour hex D8D6D4. Shot on a macro lens at high magnification, clinical and unretouched, every pore real.
